what_worked: Three-act structure provides a recognizable narrative arc with a clear audience in mind.
fix_next: Replace stock dashboard imagery and generic claims with actual dataset charts, specific numbers, and evidence-backed analysis from the 1,000 rows.
verdict: Mostly narrative filler with almost no data evidence on the slides.
factual_error_detail: Slide 7: Stripe shown as 72% of companies—actual is ~63.6% (636/1000); RevenueCat shown as 18%—actual ~18.9% (189/1000) is close but Lemon Squeezy at 6% overstates (actual 2.5%, 25/1000); Dodo Payments (50 companies, 5%) is omitted entirely and lumped into 'Paddle/Others' at 4%. Slide 4: 'over 85% of high-earning indie SaaS checkouts' is vague but Stripe's share by company count is 63.6%, not 85%; the 85.7% figure applies only to US companies. Slide 6: '$3.5M+ Top Monthly Revenue' is unverifiable from the dataset which reports 30-day revenue with a total of ~$15.6M across 1,000 companies.

evidence.insight: Claims on slides 3, 6, 10 are generic advice ('solve proven problems,' 'prioritize distribution') not derived from specific data findings; no category-level median/mean analysis, no discussion of zero-revenue prevalence (216 companies), no missingness acknowledgment.
evidence.narrative: Three-act structure (Gold Rush → Reality Check → Compass) is coherent in concept, but Act II has only two content slides (6-7) and Act III is a product pitch (slide 9) rather than data synthesis. The arc is more marketing funnel than analytical story.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 names 1,000 startups and TrustMRR but never defines the dataset scope, time period, what 'verified' means, or limitations. No mention of 274 missing categories or 241 missing countries. Audience is implied (indie builders) but analytical question is vague.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 7 provider percentages are materially wrong (Stripe 72% vs actual 63.6%; Lemon Squeezy 6% vs actual 2.5%). Slide 6 '$3.5M+' figure is unverifiable. Slide 4 '85%' claim conflates US-specific stat with overall. No denominators or sample sizes shown anywhere.
evidence.visual: Slide 4 uses a Geckoboard stock dashboard screenshot that has nothing to do with the dataset—activation rate, retention, widgets metrics are irrelevant. Slide 11 uses a stock photo. Slide 7's bar chart is the only original data visualization in the entire deck, and its numbers are wrong. Three slides (13-15) are image source citations with broken placeholder thumbnails. Heavy visual sameness across dark slides.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive consulting-style language ('undeniable heavyweight,' 'explosive mobile subscription economy,' 'category-defining outliers'); stock Geckoboard dashboard screenshot passed off as relevant evidence on slide 4; generic three-card layout on slide 9 with icon decorations; motivational closing slide 12 with no data.
